packet.headline_seed: US sanctions Rwanda gold refinery accused of smuggling DR Congo's minerals
packet.description_seed: The US alleges Gasabo Gold Refinery smuggled at least 60kg of gold in early 2026.

what: US sanctions Rwanda gold refinery accused of smuggling DR Congo's minerals

clean_source_blocks.text: The sanctions target Rwanda's Gasabo Gold Refinery The US has sanctioned a major gold refinery in Rwanda and two of its executives, accusing them of smuggling minerals from rebel-controlled areas of neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. Washington alleged what it described as a "network" was collaborating with the M23 rebel group, which commands tracts of DR Congo that are home to vast reserves of gold and coltan, a metallic ore key to making electronics. Despite overwhelming evidence from the likes of UN experts, Rwanda has long denied supporting the M23. The government there has not responded to the US' recent sanctions, but have previously described similar measures against Rwanda as unfair and one-sided. The sanctions, announced on Thursday, target the Gasabo Gold Refinery, its chairman Jean Malic Kalima and its general manager Bosco Kayobotsi.

Treasury targets Rwandan refinery and its leadership for laundering conflict gold linked to the M23 armed group in eastern DRC The US Treasury just dropped sanctions on a Rwandan gold refinery accused of laundering conflict minerals stolen from eastern Congo. Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD, along with several associated entities and individuals, is now blocked from doing business with any US person or institution. The action, taken on June 25, 2026, by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), represents one of the most significant enforcement moves targeting the illicit gold trade flowing out of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In English: if you’re a US-based company, bank, or individual, touching Gasabo Gold or its network is now a federal offense.

OFAC designated Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD under Executive Order 13413, which specifically targets entities undermining peace and stability in the DRC. The refinery, based in Kigali, Rwanda, was established on May 26, 2022, and is accused of serving as a critical laundering hub for gold extracted from mines controlled by the M23 armed group in South Kivu. The sanctions didn’t stop at the corporate entity. Chairman Jean Malic Kalima and General Manager Bosco Kayobotsi, who control the refinery’s operations, were both individually designated. Their personal assets subject to US jurisdiction are now frozen, and US persons are prohibited from transacting with them. Two additional companies were swept into the action: Bugambira Mines LTD and Wolfram Mining and Processing LTD. Both are alleged to be part of the broader network facilitating illegal mineral extraction and trade in the region.

In a statement, the US alleged at least 60kg of gold, valued at millions of US dollars, were smuggled from eastern DR Congo to Gasabo Gold in early 2026. The statement accuses Rwandan government officials and soldiers of overseeing the system. Last year, Gasabo Gold Refinery was sanctioned by the European Union for "exploiting the armed conflict" in DR Congo. Three separate mining companies controlled by Kalima - Bugambira Mines, Wolfram Mining and Processing and Rwinkwavu Mining Corporation - were also sanctioned by the US on Thursday. The sanctioned parties have not responded to the BBC's requests for comment. Any assets they have under US jurisdiction will be frozen. The sanctions also bar American citizens and companies from dealing with the designated parties.

payload.title: Yhdysvallat määräsi pakotteita ruandalaiselle kultajalostamolle
payload.summary: Yhdysvallat syyttää Gasabo Gold Refineryä Kongon demokraattisesta tasavallasta salakuljetetun kullan käsittelystä ja jäädyttää pakotteiden kohteiden Yhdysvaltojen lainkäyttöpiirissä olevat varat.
payload.content:
Yhdysvallat on määrännyt pakotteita ruandalaiselle Gasabo Gold Refinery -kultajalostamolle sekä sen johdolle osana toimia, jotka kohdistuvat Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan mineraalikauppaan. Washingtonin mukaan jalostamo oli osa verkostoa, joka salakuljetti mineraaleja kapinallisryhmien hallitsemilta alueilta Ruandaan.

## Pakotteet kohdistuvat jalostamoon ja sen johtoon

Pakotteiden kohteena ovat Kigalissa toimiva Gasabo Gold Refinery, sen puheenjohtaja Jean Malic Kalima ja toimitusjohtaja Bosco Kayobotsi. Yhdysvaltain viranomaisten mukaan jalostamo toimi keskeisenä kanavana kullalle, jota oli louhittu M23-aseellisen ryhmän hallitsemilta alueilta Itä-Kongossa.

Yhdysvaltain valtiovarainministeriön alainen pakoteviranomainen OFAC asetti jalostamon pakotelistalle presidentin asetuksen 13413 nojalla. Asetus koskee toimijoita, joiden katsotaan horjuttavan Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan rauhaa ja vakautta. Käytännössä pakotteet jäädyttävät kohteiden Yhdysvaltojen lainkäyttöpiirissä olevat varat ja kieltävät yhdysvaltalaisia henkilöitä ja yrityksiä käymästä kauppaa niiden kanssa.

Yhdysvaltojen mukaan vähintään 60 kiloa kultaa, arvoltaan miljoonia dollareita, salakuljetettiin Itä-Kongosta Gasabo Goldille alkuvuonna 2026. Viranomaiset syyttävät lausunnossaan myös ruandalaisia hallinnon edustajia ja sotilaita järjestelmän valvonnasta.

## Kiista kytkeytyy M23-ryhmään

M23 hallitsee alueita Kongon demokraattisen tasavallan itäosassa, jossa on merkittäviä kulta- ja koltaanivarantoja. Koltaani on elektroniikkateollisuudelle tärkeä malmi. YK:n asiantuntijat ovat aiemmin esittäneet näyttöä Ruandan tuesta M23:lle, mutta Ruanda on pitkään kiistänyt tukevansa ryhmää.

Ruandan hallitus ei ole vastannut tuoreisiin pakotteisiin. Se on aiemmin kuvannut vastaavia Ruandaan kohdistuneita toimia epäoikeudenmukaisiksi ja yksipuolisiksi. Pakotteiden kohteet eivät myöskään ole vastanneet BBC:n kommenttipyyntöihin.

## Myös kaivosyhtiöitä listattiin

Yhdysvallat asetti pakotteita myös Kaliman hallitsemille kaivosyhtiöille Bugambira Minesille, Wolfram Mining and Processingille ja Rwinkwavu Mining Corporationille. Lähdeaineiston mukaan Bugambira Mines ja Wolfram Mining and Processing liitetään laajempaan verkostoon, jonka väitetään helpottaneen laitonta mineraalien louhintaa ja kauppaa alueella.

Euroopan unioni määräsi Gasabo Gold Refinerylle pakotteita jo viime vuonna syyttäen sitä Kongon aseellisen konfliktin hyödyntämisestä. Yhdysvaltain tuoreet toimet laajentavat painetta jalostamoon, sen johtoon ja siihen kytkettyihin yhtiöihin.

Viranomaisten mukaan vähintään 60 kiloa kultaa salakuljetettiin Itä-Kongosta Ruandaan alkuvuonna 2026.
Pakotteet jäädyttävät Yhdysvaltojen lainkäyttöpiirissä olevat varat ja kieltävät yhdysvaltalaisia toimimasta kohteiden kanssa.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin lähdeaineistossa esitettyihin Yhdysvaltain viranomaisten väitteisiin ja pakotteiden kuvaukseen. Ruandan hallituksen ja pakotteiden kohteiden tuoreita kommentteja ei ollut aineistossa saatavilla.

article.source_text:
The sanctions target Rwanda's Gasabo Gold Refinery The US has sanctioned a major gold refinery in Rwanda and two of its executives, accusing them of smuggling minerals from rebel-controlled areas of neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo. Washington alleged what it described as a "network" was collaborating with the M23 rebel group, which commands tracts of DR Congo that are home to vast reserves of gold and coltan, a metallic ore key to making electronics. Despite overwhelming evidence from the likes of UN experts, Rwanda has long denied supporting the M23. The government there has not responded to the US' recent sanctions, but have previously described similar measures against Rwanda as unfair and one-sided. The sanctions, announced on Thursday, target the Gasabo Gold Refinery, its chairman Jean Malic Kalima and its general manager Bosco Kayobotsi.

Treasury targets Rwandan refinery and its leadership for laundering conflict gold linked to the M23 armed group in eastern DRC The US Treasury just dropped sanctions on a Rwandan gold refinery accused of laundering conflict minerals stolen from eastern Congo. Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD, along with several associated entities and individuals, is now blocked from doing business with any US person or institution. The action, taken on June 25, 2026, by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), represents one of the most significant enforcement moves targeting the illicit gold trade flowing out of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In English: if you’re a US-based company, bank, or individual, touching Gasabo Gold or its network is now a federal offense.

OFAC designated Gasabo Gold Refinery LTD under Executive Order 13413, which specifically targets entities undermining peace and stability in the DRC. The refinery, based in Kigali, Rwanda, was established on May 26, 2022, and is accused of serving as a critical laundering hub for gold extracted from mines controlled by the M23 armed group in South Kivu. The sanctions didn’t stop at the corporate entity. Chairman Jean Malic Kalima and General Manager Bosco Kayobotsi, who control the refinery’s operations, were both individually designated. Their personal assets subject to US jurisdiction are now frozen, and US persons are prohibited from transacting with them. Two additional companies were swept into the action: Bugambira Mines LTD and Wolfram Mining and Processing LTD. Both are alleged to be part of the broader network facilitating illegal mineral extraction and trade in the region.

In a statement, the US alleged at least 60kg of gold, valued at millions of US dollars, were smuggled from eastern DR Congo to Gasabo Gold in early 2026. The statement accuses Rwandan government officials and soldiers of overseeing the system. Last year, Gasabo Gold Refinery was sanctioned by the European Union for "exploiting the armed conflict" in DR Congo. Three separate mining companies controlled by Kalima - Bugambira Mines, Wolfram Mining and Processing and Rwinkwavu Mining Corporation - were also sanctioned by the US on Thursday. The sanctioned parties have not responded to the BBC's requests for comment. Any assets they have under US jurisdiction will be frozen. The sanctions also bar American citizens and companies from dealing with the designated parties.
